name: "[CI] Tests"

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, master, develop]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, master, develop]

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: 0
  CARGO_NET_RETRY: 10
  RUSTUP_MAX_RETRIES: 10
  RUST_BACKTRACE: short

jobs:
  tests_postgres:
    name: Tests (Postgres)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:15
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: postgres
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: postgres
          POSTGRES_DB: postgres
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
        ports:
          - 5432:5432

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install Rust toolchain
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - name: Restore Rust cache
        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          save-if: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' }}

      - name: Install just
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2
        with:
          tool: just
          checksum: true

      - name: Install Diesel CLI
        uses: baptiste0928/cargo-install@v3.3.0
        with:
          crate: diesel_cli
          features: postgres
          args: --no-default-features

      - name: Install cargo-nextest
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-nextest
          checksum: true

      - name: Run tests
        shell: bash
        run: just test

# Transaction and Staging Entry Overview API

## Aggregation Semantics
<!-- AI-UPDATED: 2026-06-26 - DB-derived Missing kept; time-series restored to time_range buckets + zero-fill -->
- Transaction summary endpoints are `GET /overview/transactions` (grouped by rule) and `GET /overview/transactions/rule_account_breakdown` (grouped by rule + configured account); their `time_range` requires `start_time` (with optional `end_time`) and filters by **`transaction.effective_at`** — for `/overview/transactions/rule_account_breakdown` that means the *parent transaction's* timestamp, not the entry's. Since `transaction.effective_at` is the min of its entries', a late entry is still pulled in alongside its transaction; the filter is deliberately transaction-scoped so a transaction's entries move in and out of range as a unit and the range agrees with the `missing` cutoff below (also on `transaction.effective_at`).
- The only time-series endpoint is `GET /overview/transactions/time_series`; `time_range` and `granularity` are required. The other summary endpoints have no time-series variant.
- The DB aggregates per bucket with `date_trunc(granularity, effective_at)` (`hour`/`day`/`week`/`month`) so raw rows are never shipped. Diesel can't `GROUP BY` a computed expression, so the per-bucket aggregation uses window functions partitioned by the bucket + `DISTINCT` (`aggregate_time_series_status_counts_by_rule`). The app separately builds the bucket **axis** (`OverviewTimeBuckets`, capped at `MAX_BUCKETS`) to supply each bucket's `start`/`end` and to zero-fill; the two are complementary, not redundant.
- `Missing` is not stored: a transaction is `expected` until its `effective_at` is older than the rule's aging cutoff (`AgingConfig::missing_before(now())`). The queries return per group the totals **and** the missing subset (`effective_at < cutoff` conditional aggregates — same predicate the paginated list uses, see `transaction_is_missing_expression`); the `Missing`/`Expected` split (`missing` = subset, `expected` = total − subset) is finished in the presentation layer (`ForeignTryFrom<TransactionOverviewRow> for Vec<TransactionStatusAmount>` in `utils::overview`), not the query. Because the cutoff is a per-rule instant tied to the current date, a single bucket can report both `missing` and `expected`.
<!-- AI-UPDATED: 2026-06-29 - bucket helpers moved to overview extension trait with typed errors -->
- **App and DB bucket alignment must match:** `GranularityExt` in `recon::utils::overview` snaps exactly like Postgres `date_trunc` (Monday weeks, 1st-of-month, midnight days, top-of-hour), because the DB row's `date_trunc` start is the lookup key into the `positions` map. Keep these fallible helpers in the overview layer, not on `common_enums::Granularity`, so they can return `OverviewResult`/`OverviewError` directly. A lookup miss is still treated as a bug: `position_for` returns `Option` and the core returns `InternalServerError` rather than misbucketing (which would corrupt counts). The core resolves open-ended `end_time` once and passes the resulting `DefinedTimeRange` to both the axis and the query, so they can't disagree at a boundary.

## Filtering
<!-- AI-UPDATED: 2026-07-14 - rule_ids supported across transaction overview endpoints -->
- All three transaction endpoints (`/overview/transactions`, `/overview/transactions/time_series`, `/overview/transactions/rule_account_breakdown`) accept an optional `rule_ids` query param (`OverviewFilters`/`TimeSeriesFilters` in `api_models::overview`, `OverviewFilters` shared by `/overview/transactions` and `/overview/transactions/rule_account_breakdown`): comma-separated rule IDs, parsed with `parse_comma_separated` the same way `credit_account`/`debit_account` are on `ApiTransactionAccountFilters` (plural name, unlike that struct's singular `rule_id`, since this one accepts a list).
- **Transactions / time-series** (`aggregate_status_counts_by_rule` / `aggregate_time_series_status_counts_by_rule` in `diesel_models::query::transaction`): `rule_ids` is pushed down into the SQL `WHERE` clause as `dsl::rule_id.eq_any(rule_ids)` directly on the `transaction` table, since `transaction.rule_id` is a native column. The rules list is also fetched with `list_recon_rules_by_ids(profile_id, rule_ids)` instead of `list_recon_rules_by_profile_id` when the filter is present — no fetch-all-then-discard — which is what makes the response contain only the requested rules instead of every rule zero-filled. Keep both narrowings in sync if this logic changes.
- **Rule accounts** (`aggregate_status_counts_by_rule_and_account` in `diesel_models::query::transaction`): `entry` has no `rule_id` column — only the parent `transaction` does, keyed by `entry.logical_transaction_id = transaction.transaction_id AND entry.transaction_version = transaction.version`. The query `INNER JOIN`s `transaction` on that composite key and pushes `rule_ids` down as `transaction.rule_id.eq_any(rule_ids)`. The rules list is also narrowed with `list_recon_rules_by_ids` when the filter is present, but the per-rule account set comes from the rule strategy's `get_rule_accounts()`, so **every account configured on a matching rule still appears**, zero-filled if none of its entries match. The `(logical_transaction_id, transaction_version)` join is backed by the composite index of the same name on `entry`, replacing the two single-column indexes; the standalone `transaction_version` index was not useful on its own. Archived versions are excluded from **every** transaction overview aggregate (`transaction.status != Archived` on the summary, time-series, and rule-accounts queries): every edit leaves an archived version behind (~1 per active transaction) and archived analytics are unused. Archived exclusion is enforced in two places: the query drops the real rows, and the shared zero-fill (`zero_filled_transaction_status_breakdown_with_currency`) skips `Archived` so it is not re-added as a phantom `0`. Therefore, `Archived` never appears in any `status_breakdown`.
- No existence check on `rule_ids`: rule IDs from another profile, or that don't exist, are silently dropped, yielding an empty (or partial/zero-filled) response, not a 404 — same "don't leak cross-profile existence" pattern used elsewhere.

## Staging Entry Overview
<!-- AI-UPDATED: 2026-07-14 - GET /overview/staging_entries added -->
- `GET /overview/staging_entries` groups staging-entry statuses by account. Its `time_range` is mandatory (`StagingEntryOverviewFilters.time_range: TimeRange`), so a query without `start_time` gets a 400 instead of an unbounded aggregate.
- Two independent filters, each narrowing a different axis: `account_ids` narrows the **account list itself** (fetched via `list_accounts_by_profile_id_and_account_ids` instead of `list_accounts_by_profile_id` when present — same no-fetch-all-then-discard principle as `rule_ids`), while `transformation_history_ids` only narrows the **aggregation** — every selected account still appears, zero-filled, since an account isn't owned by a single transformation run.
<!-- AI-UPDATED: 2026-08-04 - detailed_status_breakdown added alongside the coarse one -->
- **Two breakdowns per account, from the same rows.** The SQL aggregate groups by the granular `staging_entry.status`, so `detailed_status_breakdown` (`StagingEntryDetailedStatusAmount`, one row per `DieselStagingEntryStatus`) is the direct mapping of the query result, and `status_breakdown` (`StagingEntryStatusAmount`, coarse) is a fold that re-keys those rows on `(ApiStagingEntryStatus::coarse(), currency)` and **sums** them — the ten `needs_manual_review_*` reasons collapse into one `needs_manual_review` bucket. Don't compute the coarse one with a second query. `status_breakdown` dies in step 2 of the status swap (see the transactions `AGENT-NOTES.md` section on the 2-step swap), `detailed_status_breakdown` stays.
- Both zero-fill their whole enum minus `Archived` — 4 rows and 13 rows per account respectively (only `NeedsManualReview` is granular, so the detailed breakdown is the ten reasons plus `Pending`/`Processed`/`Void`) — so an account with no entries still returns a complete breakdown. No `Missing`/aging split, since staging entries don't carry the rule-aging concept transactions do. `Archived` rows are excluded at the query level (`dsl::status.ne(Archived)`, same as `list_v2_paginated`'s default): archived rows are superseded prior *versions* of a staging entry (e.g. the pre-void version, or one consumed into a matched transaction), not distinct entities worth counting — every void produces one, so leaving them in would double-count.
- **`StagingEntryDetailedStatusAmount` flattens its status, `GetStagingEntryResponse` does not.** The breakdown struct has no sibling `status` key, so `#[serde(flatten)]` on the adjacently-tagged `ApiStagingEntryStatus` is safe and its entries serialize as `{"status": …, "sub_status": …, "count": …}` — i.e. the Rust field is `detailed_status` but the wire key is `status`. `GetStagingEntryResponse` can't flatten (its coarse `status` would collide), so there it nests. Both are deliberate; see the transactions `AGENT-NOTES.md`.
- Response includes `account_type` (the account's `BalanceDirection`) alongside `account_id`/`account_name`, as does the transaction rule-account breakdown.

## Response Shape Gotchas
<!-- AI-UPDATED: 2026-07-16 - rule_account_breakdown counts credit/debit separately -->
- `/overview/transactions/rule_account_breakdown` uses `AccountTransactionStatusAmount` (`credit_count`/`debit_count`), not the shared `TransactionStatusAmount` (`count`) used by the other two transaction endpoints. A single account can carry both a credit-direction and a debit-direction entry from the *same* transaction (e.g. a clearing account) — a deduplicated overall count would silently collapse that down to 1. Computed in `aggregate_status_counts_by_rule_and_account` via `count(case_when(balance_direction = ..., id)).aggregate_distinct()`, mirroring the existing `sum(case_when(...))` pattern already used for `credit_amount`/`debit_amount`. Don't widen the shared `TransactionStatusAmount` to add this — the rule-level and time-series responses have no per-account entry split, so a transaction only ever contributes once there.
<!-- AI-UPDATED: 2026-07-14 - Archived excluded from all overview endpoints (query + zero-fill) -->
<!-- AI-UPDATED: 2026-06-26 - time-series buckets carry time_range {start,end} and are zero-filled across the whole range -->
- Transaction summaries (`/overview/transactions`, `/overview/transactions/rule_account_breakdown`) include every recon rule / configured account and zero-fill the full transaction status enum except `Archived` (which every overview query drops), so empty owners still come back with a complete `status_breakdown`.
- Each transaction time-series bucket carries a `time_range` (`start_time`/`end_time`, clipped to the request) and a `status_breakdown` zero-filled to the full transaction status enum except `Archived`. Every bucket in the range is emitted (including empty ones, fully zeroed), so every bucket has the same shape.
- All responses use `status_breakdown` arrays, not status-keyed objects.
- Amounts are `AmountResponse` values, and aggregation remains grouped by currency, so a status may appear more than once if matching rows span currencies.

# Manual Reconciliation (Exception Management)

> Read with `AGENT-NOTES.md`. Covers both versions of the human-driven reconcile endpoint:
> `POST /exception_management/transactions/{id}/manual_reconciliation` (v1) and `.../manual_reconciliation/v2`.
> Core: `recon/src/core/exception_management.rs`. Entry builders: `recon/src/domain/exception_management/manual_reconciliation.rs`.
> Validations: `recon/src/utils/exception_management.rs` (`EntryOpsVecExt` over the ops, `PreparedEntryVecExt` over the built entries).

## Why v2 exists
<!-- AI-UPDATED: 2026-09-22 - Delta reconciliation endpoint -->
- **v1's payload has no entry id.** `TransactionEntryWithData` carries no `entry_id`, so the server cannot tell an edited entry from an untouched one: it archives every entry and rebuilds the whole set from whatever the client sent. With `MAX_ENTRIES_PER_TRANSACTION` at 25 000 (`recon/src/domain/transaction.rs`) the FE would have to hold the full set in memory and ship it back on every call, while its own entry list APIs page at 50.
- **v2 takes operations on individual entries instead.** Untouched entries never appear on the wire; the server re-creates them itself from the rows it already read. `{id}` is the per-version PK, so the request names one specific version.
- **v1 stays registered and none of the fixes below were backported** — an FE on v1 still gets v1's behaviour. It is slated for deprecation (a `TODO` in `manual_transaction_reconciliation`) but not marked deprecated in code or OpenAPI. One visible change did reach it: `InvalidEntryStatus` now names an entry, v1 has no entry id to give, so its 400 message reads `with id: ""`.

## Three things v1 silently loses, and v2 does not
- **`exposed_metadata` is written as `json!({})`** on every entry v1 rebuilds. That field is what entry list filters and reporting read, so a manually reconciled transaction drops out of metadata-filtered views. v2 projects it for real (see the fresh/carried rule below).
- **Re-sent entries lose `primary_staging_entry_id` and `transformation_config_id`.** v1 filters already-`Processed` staging entries out of its lookup map, so both resolve to `None`.
- **…which strands their `search_duplicate` rows as `Archived`.** `EntryNew::batch_insert_chunked` reactivates a duplicate *only* for entries that carry a `primary_staging_entry_id` (`diesel_models/src/query/entry.rs`), so an entry that lost the field never comes back to `Active`. Dropping that field anywhere in a versioning flow has this effect — it is not specific to manual recon.
- **Neither v1 nor `force_reconcile`/void/post re-emits `search_entry_key` rows**, so searchable metadata kept pointing at the superseded version. v2 writes them for the new version (see below).

## The operations (`EntryOp`, internally tagged on `op`)
| Op | Effect |
|---|---|
| `update_entry` | apply `EntryOverrides` to an existing entry |
| `mark_received` | an `Expected` entry arrived → `Pending`; target must currently be `Expected` |
| `create_entry` | add a `NewEntry::Direct` or `NewEntry::Expected` |
| `create_with_staging_entry` | pull an unreconciled staging entry in as a new entry |
| `replace_with_staging_entry` | drop the named entry *and* add the staging-sourced one; net count delta zero |
| `remove_entry` | drop an entry |

- **The account is fixed; the amount is not.** `EntryOverrides` (`update_entry`, `mark_received`) can change `amount`, `entry_type`, `effective_at`, `metadata`, `order_id` and `transformation_id` on any existing entry, staging-sourced ones included, but has no `account_id`: v1 moves an entry by resending it on another account, and v2 dropped that in review. New entries name their account; staging-sourced entries take the staging row's.
- **Unknown keys are dropped, not rejected** (no `deny_unknown_fields`). An `account_id` in `EntryOverrides`, an `amount` in `StagingEntryOverrides` or a `transformation_id` on `kind: expected` is ignored, and the call still succeeds.
- **An op's `staging_entry_id` is the staging row's primary `id`** (per version, `GetStagingEntryResponse.id`), not its logical `staging_entry_id` — `prepare_staging_links` filters on `id`, as v1 does.
- Accepted transaction statuses: the nine in `MANUALLY_RECONCILABLE_STATUSES`. Anything else is a 400 `InvalidTransactionStatus`. v1 hand-lists the same nine in a `match`, so change both together.
- Only `mark_received` checks the target entry's status. `update_entry`, `remove_entry` and `replace_with_staging_entry` take the entry in whatever status the loaded version holds; the reasoning given in review is that entry statuses follow the transaction's, which is already restricted to those nine.
- **Payload validation is pure** (`EntryOpsVecExt::validate_payload`, no I/O) and runs before any entry is loaded: non-empty ops (`EmptyEntryOps`), every `entry_id`/`staging_entry_id` named at most once across the whole request (`DuplicateEntryOpTarget`), the entry cap, and amounts. `replace_with_staging_entry` contributes **both** of its ids to the duplicate check.
  - **The cap is computed from the transaction row**: its `entry_ids`, minus `remove_entry` targets, plus one per `create_entry`/`create_with_staging_entry`, against `MAX_ENTRIES_PER_TRANSACTION` → 400 `TooManyEntries`. So an oversized request fails before the entry load and before any encrypt or decrypt.
  - **Amounts are checked in minor units of the transaction currency**, for `create_entry` and `EntryOverrides.amount` alike. The float→minor conversion truncates, so `0.001` USD is 0 minor units and a 400 `InvalidAmount`, even though it is positive as a float.
- **The resulting entry set must still cover every account on the transaction's rule** (`PreparedEntryVecExt::validate_rule_account_coverage`, against `rule.strategy.get_recon_engine_type().get_rule_accounts()`) → 400 `MissingRuleAccountEntries` listing what is missing. This is what stops `remove_entry` from emptying a transaction: a zero-entry version is trivially balanced with no `Expected` entries, so without the check it would be written as `Matched(Manual)`, with `new_versioned` falling back to `now()` for its `effective_at`. Note a rule that *gains* an account after a transaction was created makes that transaction fail this check until an entry for the new account is added — which the endpoint itself can do with `create_entry`.
- The rule is fetched **before** the write (it is also what supplies `aging_config` for the response), so a missing rule is a 404 instead of a failure after a successful commit.
- Resulting status: any surviving `Expected` entry, or credits ≠ debits → `PartiallyReconciled`. Otherwise `Matched(Manual)` — and **every** entry in the new version, carried-forward ones included, is rewritten to `EntryStatus::Matched`.

## The rule that governs metadata: fresh vs carried
`exposed_metadata` is the entry's metadata projected through its transformation config's schema, and the `search_entry_key` rows are derived from that projection. Both are recomputed **exactly when the entry is new or an op supplies `metadata` or `transformation_id` for it**, never otherwise — a schema edit alone does not refresh a carried entry:

| case | metadata ciphertext | `exposed_metadata` | search keys |
|---|---|---|---|
| untouched entry, or an op supplying neither `metadata` nor `transformation_id` | copied | copied | copied from the rows fetched for the old entry |
| op supplies `metadata` | re-encrypted | re-projected | re-derived |
| op supplies `transformation_id` only | copied (decrypted only to project) | re-projected | re-derived |
| `create_entry` / staging-sourced entry | encrypted from the request, or the staging entry's ciphertext reused | projected, or the staging entry's copied | derived |

- **An untouched entry is never decrypted.** Every decrypt is bounded by the request: one per op that supplies `transformation_id` without `metadata`, and one per linked staging entry (`convert_back` in `prepare_staging_links`, which `build_search_duplicate` needs). Representing an entry as `DomainEntry` forces a decrypt, because `EncryptableValue` holds plaintext *and* ciphertext — that is why this flow works on `diesel_models::EntryNew` and not the domain type. At 25 000 entries a decrypt-per-entry pass is 25 000 key-manager round trips.
- **`PreparedEntry::projected` derives the search keys from the entry's own `exposed_metadata`**, so the two cannot disagree; `PreparedEntry::carried` is the copy path. Anything that builds an entry goes through one of the two.
- An entry with no transformation config projects through `NO_EXPOSED_KEYS` (`common_types::metadata_schema`) — i.e. `{}` — which is also what `create_entry` with `kind: expected` gets.

## Why the existing search keys are fetched
`load_existing_entries_with_search_keys` reads the version's entries **and** their `search_entry_key` rows into one `HashMap<entry_id, ExistingEntry>` that everything downstream uses.
- **It bounds the config/schema fetch by the request, not by the transaction.** Untouched entries carry their keys over verbatim, so their transformation configs are never needed. Re-deriving instead would require the `ExposedKeys` of every config referenced across all 25 000 entries, and a config that has since been deleted would fail the whole call.
- Updates and receipts fetch configs only when `metadata` or `transformation_id` is supplied.
- The fetch is `list_search_entry_keys_by_entry_ids_and_profile_id` with no limit, which rides `idx_sek_entry_id`. There is **no index on `search_entry_key.primary_transaction_id`**, so fetching a version's keys by that single column would seq-scan until a migration adds one. It takes the ids by value and logs only their count on error; logging the ids would put up to 25 000 of them in one line.
- Consequence to keep in mind: if a schema's `searchable` list changed after those entries were written, a carried-forward entry keeps the keys the old schema produced. That is consistent with its copied `exposed_metadata`.

## Overriding `transformation_id` forces a decrypt
`EntryOverrides.transformation_id` re-classifies an entry under a different config. The stored `exposed_metadata` was projected through the *old* schema and cannot be reused, and it cannot be re-projected from itself either — the new schema may expose keys the old projection dropped. So that entry's metadata is decrypted (`EncryptionHandler::decrypt_json_value`) purely to re-project; the ciphertext is stored back unchanged. This is bounded by the ops in the request, never by the entry count.
- **Supplying the id the entry already has still re-projects, on purpose.** The trigger is "the op supplied a `transformation_id`", not "the id changed", because a config's `metadata_schema_id` can be repointed and the schema itself edited — so the same config id can mean a different projection than the one stored. Sending the current id is the way to ask for a refresh.
- **The config must belong to the entry's account** → 400 `TransformationConfigAccountMismatch`.
  `EntryOpsVecExt::transformations_to_validate` checks config overrides against the existing entry's
  immutable account, and checks `create_entry`'s config against its requested account.
- A config id that does not resolve in the profile is a **404** `TransformationConfigNotFound` (RE_619). That variant was a 400 before v2, and the change also reaches `POST /transactions`, its only other raiser (`exposed_keys_for_entry`).
- **`StagingEntryOverrides` has only `effective_at`, `metadata` and `order_id`.** A link takes the account, `entry_type`, amount and `transformation_id` from the staging row, so the new entry starts out as what was ingested. Nothing keeps it that way: `EntryOverrides` allows amount, `entry_type` and `transformation_id`, so a later request can `update_entry` the linked entry (not the same request — its id is generated server-side). The staging row stays `Processed` for its full amount, and nothing flags that the entry no longer matches it. Only the account can never diverge.

## `search_entry_key` conventions
- `primary_transaction_id` is the **version PK** (`transaction.id`), not the logical `transaction_id` — same as `TransactionCreationData::get_new_transaction_data` uses on the creation path. Keys are therefore minted *after* the new transaction row is built, inside the same DB transaction.
- Rows are never deleted anywhere in the codebase. Superseded versions keep theirs; queries scope by `entry_id`, and archived entries' ids simply stop being current.

## Structure and cost
- Ops are indexed once by target entry id (`HashMap<&str, &EntryOp>`) and the entry set is walked once. Searching the entry vec per op instead is O(entries × ops), and `Vec::retain` per removal makes it worse — that shape was removed deliberately.
- The entry set is loaded whole and every entry is rewritten, exactly like `force_reconcile`, void, post and the engine flows. The O(N) write amplification is inherent to the versioning model and is not solved here; this endpoint solves the API contract only.
- **Entry order in a new version is undefined.** `Entry::list_by_transaction_id_and_version` has no `ORDER BY`, and v2 additionally iterates a `HashMap` under `buffer_unordered`. Do not write anything that depends on `entry_ids` ordering.
- Configs and schemas for linked staging entries are fetched twice — once in `prepare_staging_links` (which needs the full rows for `build_search_duplicate`) and once in `MetadataProjection::resolve`.
- **Crypto is per op, not batched.** Each encrypt, decrypt and staging `convert_back` is its own call (a key-manager round trip under `KeymanagerService`), `PREPARATION_MAX_CONCURRENT` (5) at a time. That is fine for FE-sized requests, but it is not the batch pattern CRITICAL-PATHS asks of transformations, and only the entry cap bounds the op count.

## Known gaps (intentional or deferred)
- **No concurrency control.** There is no row lock and no 409: if the version moves between the client reading it and saving, the write proceeds against the stale snapshot, and a losing `UNIQUE (transaction_id, version)` race surfaces as a 500. A live version is also mutable in place — `Transaction::append_expected_source_entry` rewrites `entry_ids` and the aggregates at the *same* version — so "version unchanged" does not mean "nothing changed". Two requests linking the same staging entry race the same way: `uniq_idx_staging_entry_id_version` makes the loser a 500, not a double link.
- **`search_expectation`s are archived and never recreated** on any manual path. A transaction a human has edited leaves the recon engine's automatic flow by design; late arrivals land in `NeedsManualReview`.
- **`remove_entry` and `replace_with_staging_entry` do not release the dropped entry's staging entry**: it stays `Processed` and its `search_duplicate` stays `Archived`.
- Validation errors reuse `EntryNotFound` (404) and `InvalidEntryStatus` (400) rather than v2-specific variants. The five variants v2 added — `TooManyEntries`, `EmptyEntryOps`, `DuplicateEntryOpTarget`, `TransformationConfigAccountMismatch`, `MissingRuleAccountEntries` — are RE_620–624, all 400.

# File Storage - Agent Notes

## Common Gotchas
<!-- AI-UPDATED: 2025-01-04 - Multipart upload implementation -->
- S3 bucket must exist before file uploads work - LocalStack requires manual bucket creation
<!-- AI-UPDATED: 2026-10-12 - OCI supports the same download interface -->
- Presigned URLs work with AWS S3 and OCI Object Storage; filesystem storage returns `None`
- OCI uses Customer Secret Keys via the AWS SDK credential chain; see [external-services/AGENT-NOTES.md](../external-services/AGENT-NOTES.md) for credential isolation and separate application/SFTP configuration gotchas
- File keys cannot start with '/' - S3 validation will reject them
- Multipart field names are case-sensitive: use "file", "file_name", "purpose" exactly
- MIME type detection requires file content analysis - cannot rely on filename extensions
- File size validation (10MB limit) happens after streaming, not before upload starts

## Design Decisions
<!-- AI-UPDATED: 2025-01-07 - Account-based organization -->
- Files organized by account hierarchy: `{merchant_id}/{profile_id}/{account_id}_{timestamp}/{filename}`
- Upload endpoint moved to account routes: `/accounts/{account_id}/upload_file`
- Account validation ensures file belongs to authenticated user's profile
- Timestamp combined with account_id for unique file organization
- Base64 encoding used for JSON responses to handle binary data
- File storage utils integrated into account utils for domain cohesion

## LocalStack Configuration
<!-- AI-UPDATED: 2025-01-04 - Development setup -->
- Endpoint URL: http://localhost:4566 for LocalStack
- Path style must be enabled: `path_style = true` in config
- Bucket name: hyperswitch-recon-files (must be created manually)
- AWS credentials can be dummy values for LocalStack: test/test

## Transaction Patterns
<!-- AI-UPDATED: 2024-06-24 - Added transaction pattern from recon-rules -->
```rust
// Multi-table atomic operations
async fn create_with_related_entities(
    &self,
    main_entity: MainEntityNew,
    related_entities: Vec<RelatedEntityNew>,
) -> StorageResult<(MainEntity, Vec<RelatedEntity>)> {
    use async_bb8_diesel::AsyncConnection;
    use diesel_models::errors::DatabaseError;
    use error_stack::ResultExt;

    let conn = self.get_connection().await?;

    conn.transaction_async(|connection_pool| async move {
        // Insert main entity first
        let created_main = main_entity
            .insert(&connection_pool)
            .await
            .map_err(|_| DatabaseError::Others)?;

        // Insert all related entities
        let mut created_related = Vec::new();
        for entity in related_entities {
            let created = entity
                .insert(&connection_pool)
                .await
                .map_err(|_| DatabaseError::Others)?;
            created_related.push(created);
        }

        Ok::<_, DatabaseError>((created_main, created_related))
    })
    .await
    .change_context(DatabaseError::DatabaseConnectionError)
    .attach_printable("Failed to create entities in transaction")
}
```

### Regex Implementation Details
<!-- AI-UPDATED: 2026-08-11 - Regex extraction rule now wired on datetime too -->
- **Location**: `crates/recon/src/domain/metadata_schema/transformations/regex_extract.rs` (module named `regex_extract` to avoid clash with the `regex` crate name).
- **Functions**: `regex_extract_value(value: &mut Option<String>, pattern: &str, group: Option<usize>)` and `validate_regex_config(pattern: &str, group: Option<usize>)`.
- **Currently wired on**: `StringTransformationRuleV1` and `DateTimeTransformationRuleV1`. The shared helper lives under `transformations::` so other datatypes can opt in without a second implementation — wiring a new datatype is one `ValueTransformer` arm plus one `ConfigValidator` arm.
- **Extraction Semantics**: `group: Some(n)` returns capture group `n`; `group: None` returns the whole match (`captures.get(0)`). A group that matched nothing (optional group in the pattern) surfaces as `UnmatchedRegex`, not `None`.
- **Error Surface**: `RuleError::InvalidConfig { details }` (bad pattern, wrapped compilation error) and `RuleError::UnmatchedRegex { pattern }` (input had no match). No-match is intentionally an error (parallel to `StripPrefix`/`StripSuffix`); if you need optional extraction, use two different rules or a new variant. Note: Runtime regex compilation failures should not occur since patterns are validated at config-save time via `ConfigFieldValidationError::RegexCompileFailed`.
- **Config-Time Check**: `validate_regex_config` compiles the pattern and range-checks `group`, failing fast with `ConfigFieldValidationError::RegexCompileFailed` / `RegexGroupOutOfRange`. Both `StringConfigV1::validate_config` and `DateTimeConfigV2::validate_config` iterate `transformation_rules` to reach it — keep those loops if you add more syntactically-constrained transformation rules.
- **On DateTime, regex slices but does not reformat**: the extracted substring is still parsed against the configured `date_time_format`, so the capture group must match the declared `order`/`delimiter` exactly. A pattern that pulls `22/06/2026` out of `"Totals for Payment on 22/06/2026"` needs `date_format: {order: day_month_year, delimiter: slash}` — the regex cannot rewrite separators.
- **ReDoS**: The `regex` crate guarantees linear-time matching; no catastrophic backtracking concern.

### DateTime Post-Parse Implementation Details
<!-- AI-UPDATED: 2026-04-23 - PostParseTransformer trait + split-list schema for DateTime -->
- **Location**: `crates/recon/src/domain/metadata_schema/transformations/datetime_post_parse.rs` exports `pub fn apply_truncation`, `pub fn apply_duration_addition`, `pub fn apply_duration_subtraction`. All take `&mut PrimitiveDateTime` — these are the computational primitives, not the dispatch layer.
- **Dispatch**: `PostParseTransformer` trait in `data_validator.rs` (sibling to `ValueTransformer`) with signature `fn apply_post_parse_transformation(&self, value: &mut Self::DataType) -> Result<(), Report<RuleError>>`. Impls for `DateTimePostParseTransformationRule` and `DateTimePostParseTransformationRuleV1` live in `datatypes/datetime.rs` and call into the helper module. The validator calls `post_parse_rule.apply_post_parse_transformation(&mut parsed_datetime)` as a trait method.
- **Why `&mut T` not `&mut Option<T>`**: by the time post-parse runs, the value is guaranteed present (we bailed if parse returned `None`). `ValueTransformer` uses `&mut Option<T>` because pre-parse sees raw CSV cells that can be empty.
- **Schema shape**: `DateTimeConfigV2 { format, transformation_rules, post_parse_rules }` and `EffectiveAtFieldConfigV2 { ..., transformation_rules, post_parse_rules }`. Two separate `Vec`s — the enums don't share variants, so the compiler rejects misplacing a rule between phases.
- **Non-versioned payload types**: `TruncationPrecision`, `DateTimeDuration`, `DurationUnit` are leaf payloads consumed by `DateTimePostParseTransformationRuleV1` variants. They're not versioned — the outer `DateTimePostParseTransformationRule::V1(...)` wrapping is the version boundary, same pattern as `pointer: String` inside `JsonExtract`. Additive evolution (new variants) doesn't need a version bump; breaking changes introduce `DateTimePostParseTransformationRule::V2(...)`.
- **Error model**: all three helpers return `RuleError::InvalidDateTimeConfig { details }` on failure (overflow, out-of-range calendar date). Pre-parse errors (invalid format) surface via `ValueError::InvalidFormat` from the parse step between the two phases.
